title: Counting attackers and defenders
outcomes: Counts attackers and defenders of a square and says who wins material
Captures with the cheapest piece first
Spots a pinned defender that cannot recapture
Notices when one defender has two jobs

steps.text:
Before you capture on a square, **count**. List every piece that can capture there for each side, with its value. The side that starts captures with its **cheapest** piece first, and either side may stop whenever carrying on would lose material.
Then compare: what do I win, and what do I lose?

steps.caption: White to move. Three white pieces attack e5 and two black pieces defend it.

line.say: The pawn captures first, the cheapest of the three attackers.
The knight takes the pawn on e5.
The rook takes the knight. White has won two pawns and a knight for a pawn and a knight.

claims.statement: The capture sequence on e5 wins a pawn for White along the engine line.

steps.text:
A count is only as good as its pieces.
**Order matters.** With the same numbers, a cheap piece that captures first can win what an expensive one would lose.
**Every counted piece must really be able to capture.** A pinned piece cannot recapture if that would expose its king, and a piece with two jobs may be needed elsewhere.
